title: Saudi social and livestreaming platform HooLive migrates to Tencent Cloud
html:
Saudi Arabian social audio and live-streaming platform HooLive has migrated its workloads to Tencent Cloud.

The company has moved its cloud infrastructure, databases, live-streaming, Video on Demand (VOD), and Content Delivery Network (CDN) services to Tencent Cloud, alongside a containerization upgrade designed to enhance business elasticity and operational resilience.

Tencent's VOD capabilities support the storage, management, and delivery of video content at scale for HooLive, enabling content to be recorded and replayed.

HooLive has not publicly disclosed the cloud provider it worked with prior to the migration.

Rachel Xie, GM of Tencent Cloud Middle East and GM of operations, channel development and marketing of Tencent Cloud International, said: "We are pleased to support HooLive's continued growth and innovation as one of Saudi Arabia's leading homegrown social entertainment platforms. By combining Tencent Cloud's cloud infrastructure and media technologies with HooLive's strong market presence and innovation capabilities, this collaboration helps create a stronger technology foundation that supports richer user experiences and future opportunities for development. It also reflects our commitment to helping media and entertainment companies innovate and thrive through scalable, high-performance cloud solutions."

Ahmed Farwq, CEO and owner of HooLive, added: "Providing a high-quality user experience is critical as we continue to serve millions of users across Saudi Arabia. Tencent Cloud's strong technical capabilities, responsive support, and cost-effective solutions made it the right technology partner for our next phase of growth. Through this migration, we have strengthened our technology foundation while creating greater flexibility to support future innovation and user engagement."

Tencent launched its inaugural Middle Eastern cloud region in Saudi Arabia in February 2025. At the start of this year, the company said it was "actively" exploring developing more data centers in the Middle East.

This week has also seen Tencent post its earnings results for Q3 2026. The company does not report on its cloud unit separately, but full-company revenues were RMB 207.3 billion ($31.1bn), up eight percent Year-over-Year (YoY), and gross profit was RMB 115 billion ($17.25bn), up seven percent YoY.

Capex, meanwhile, was significantly up at RMB 65.1bn ($9.77bn), up 225 percent YoY, leading to a negative free cash flow of RMB 69.1 billion. This was put down to "accelerated investment in AI infrastructure." Commenting on this, chief strategy officer James Mitchell said that they think capex is "at peak levels" and may bounce "up and down around this peak level through the rest of 2026 and 2027." It is expected to slow in 2028.

President Martin Lau noted that the company's AI offerings are growing rapidly, with its WorkBuddy application now having more than 10 million daily active users and consuming more than 100 trillion tokens daily. The application's annualized gross revenue over the last seven days has exceeded $500 million.

Regarding the cloud unit's performance, Lau later added: "We are at the early stages of adding compute capacity at an accelerated pace and making a portion of that capacity available to external paying customers through Tencent Cloud. As a result, our cloud services business is now starting to deliver financial benefits from our AI initiatives, initially from WorkBuddy, Model-as-a-Service, and GPU rentals. During the third quarter, cloud services revenue growth accelerated 35 percent year-on-year from 21 percent Year-over-Year in the second quarter, and teens-level percentage year-on-year growth throughout 2025."

Compared to Alibaba Cloud, Tencent's AI and cloud revenue growth has been much slower, with Alibaba seeing growth rates of 53 percent and 64 percent, respectively, in the most recent quarter. Tencent's strategy has thus far been to focus compute internally on developing AI tools, rather than leasing out the capacity to customers.
summary: Tencent also publishes quarterly earnings results
